The north star: the Ten-Minute Test
A sceptical stranger with ten minutes should be able to:
1. clone the repository and get green checks;
2. reproduce a published number of their choosing, change an assumption, and see why the result moves;
3. see the latest change with who built it, who checked it and what it cost;
4. read the float figures, each with its basis, and what would move them.
The target is a nightly run that does all four from a clean environment and publishes the result.
Step 1 can be run by hand: tools/stranger_[link] clones a commit, clears the environment and runs the main make check gates.
Step 3 is the public work log at [link]

Why cells, and not one big envelope
Every vacuum-balloon study in the literature analyses a single sphere, and reaches the same negative result: a shell thin enough to float buckles under one atmosphere.
Every vacuum-balloon study in the literature analyses a single sphere, and reaches the same negative result: a shell thin enough to float buckles under one atmosphere.
Akhmeteli & Gavrilin showed a perfect diamond sphere collapses at about 0.2 atm.
A single envelope carries one atmosphere across its whole shell; a cell array carries it only at the boundary.
A single envelope carries one atmosphere across its whole shell; a cell array carries it only at the boundary.
ONE ENVELOPE — every part of the shell holds 1 atm
ONE ENVELOPE — every part of the shell holds 1 atm
AN ARRAY — only the boundary holds 1 atm
interior walls: vacuum both sides, zero load

The shared wall between two sealed vacuum cells has vacuum on both sides. It carries no pressure differential at all. The atmosphere is held only at the outside of the array. Behind that outside sits a deep cellular core, so there is no thin shell left to buckle.
To float, the solid fraction of the hull must be a few parts in ten thousand.
Sizing the tube so that Euler buckling and local wall buckling fail together changes the exponent from φ² to φ1.5.
Sizing the tube so that Euler buckling and local wall buckling fail together changes the exponent from φ² to φ1.5.
SAME MASS OF MATERIAL, TWO WAYS
so lattice strength ∝ φ²
so lattice strength ∝ φ1.5
The optimum tube is the one where the strut's Euler buckling and the tube wall's local buckling arrive at the same load. Anything else is wasting material on the mode that is not governing.

A wall you can actually lay down sets a floor on how long the struts must be, and therefore on how big one cell is.
What one flooded cell costs its neighbours
Flood one cell and its shared walls have an atmosphere pushing into the vacuum next door.
Aerogel stiffness falls as roughly the cube of its density, so the two effects race each other.

Running the cells at half a vacuum halves the lift and halves the load, and buys nothing at all.

The requirement is ρshell < ρair, and ρshell scales with pressure — so what matters is ρ/p = 1/RT, a function of temperature alone.
Cold air is the only free lunch, and it is a small one.
It asks whether a cell of this architecture holds one atmosphere at the relative density predicted, and whether it fails where predicted.
The sealed-cell architecture is what turns an impossibility proof into an engineering problem, and hollow struts are what turn the engineering problem into a buildable one.

That belongs to a deep sandwich shell: two faces of fat carbon chord pipe held metres apart by web diagonals, joined by the same clamped titanium joints as the cell, only larger.

Follow the load: the sky dishes each half-metre panel of film inward, and the panel hands its pull to the rings it lies on; the rings turn roughly seventy thousand small pulls into one great hoop of compression around the barrel; the webs carry shear between the walls; the inner wall's longerons carry the caps' whole thrust down the length.

The mission cycle drawn as a loop of six phases: a flown final approach with the hose paying out, pure pumping at the water, an outbound leg that winds the hose up while climbing and lets down on arrival, the drop run along the fire, the escape climb the drop itself powers, and a return that makes nitrogen ballast while descending to hose range.
Three levers work together.
The ballast system has one job: add tonnes the Mind can dial, aboard a vehicle that is mostly made of nothing.
Buying mass there spends the one budget the project cannot spare.

But liquid air is about 21% oxygen, and it does not stay 21%.

Nitrogen boils at 77 K, oxygen at 90 K, so a standing tank boils its nitrogen off first and the liquid that remains enriches toward liquid oxygen.

Aboard this vehicle that property is disqualifying three times over:
Venting an oxygen-enriching liquid over the one thing the mission exists to smother is not a failure mode anyone should have to analyse.
Nitrogen is the boring four-fifths of every breath the intake takes.
The separation column hands the oxygen straight back to the sky rather than storing it, and its energy cost is already priced into the 0.45 kWh/kg dial in section 04.

The modest discount liquid air offers is the price of not flying a slowly concentrating oxidizer through a fire in a flammable airframe — a bad trade at any efficiency. (Argon would be denser ballast still, and just as inert, but air offers only one percent of it; nitrogen is what the sky actually stocks.)

Figure 4 Five layers between an idea and an actuator.

Five layers between an idea and an actuator: humans set objectives and hold stop authority; a strategic Mind proposes fleet allocation; regional Minds plan and deconflict; each vehicle Mind requests manoeuvres as typed proposals; a deterministic verified safety kernel decides what is permitted; bounded actuator controllers execute and fail safe.

On the live view, the monitor reads BC Wildfire Service fire points and perimeters from this site's mirror, joined by fire number. The visible live view checks the mirror every fifteen minutes. If the mirror is unavailable on entry, the monitor tries the newest captured fleet day and labels it as a dated sample. Statuses of Out are excluded. Satellite hotspots are NRCan CWFIS last-24-h detections, used only on the live view when its mirror answers. On the live view, available Open-Meteo 850 hPa winds affect transit times and target scoring. The mirror limits wind requests to once an hour. The monitor interpolates its coarse BC grid to route midpoints. Missing or stale wind means still air. Weather data by [link] (CC BY 4.0). Where the BC record supplies an official incident link, the monitor provides it. Exercise fires have no official incident page. Data, licences and notices records the sources and their terms. For a real emergency use the BC Wildfire Service, not this page. Open Government Licence – British Columbia

Drop-line targeting scores candidate lines using available wind, satellite detections and community proximity, then favours adjacent lines. The model's city list is the population proxy; parcel-level values-at-risk data would refine it. No line repeats until the plan has been treated once. First-order triage, not fire science. Source selection is a size-weighted choice among definite water bodies meeting the class's area and distance rules, larger water preferred over just-qualifying. Fleet allocation scores eligible fires by size, class fit and source distance. Also computed are routes, phase durations, pump and drag and descent power, nitrogen mass-energy cycling, and throughput. The arithmetic section explains selected formulas. The shared model holds the full configuration.

Every vehicle parameter — speeds, fill rates, hose heads, generator, battery, cryogenic and solar capacities, drag coefficients, efficiencies. The class cards label their values as conceptual assumptions. Weather: only the live view uses an available 850 hPa wind sample per route. Dated views and the exercise use still air. Routes and altitude profiles remain nominal, and no invented weather value appears anywhere on this page. The configuration records changes to the assumptions in its source comments.

That job belongs to a deep two-walled truss: heavy carbon chords in an outer and an inner wall about m apart, laced by diagonal webs, with pretensioned spokes crossing the void beyond.

The top half of the hull is decked in solar panels; the rotors sit on pylons on the horizontal beam of the ship, as far from lines and film as the geometry allows, because their hardest work is pushing up — holding the buoyant hull down against a lake while the pump drinks.

The only open-access measurement found of gas flow through as-printed FDM walls, and the basis for this project's position that the printed strut is structure, not the vacuum barrier. Caveats that ride on every number taken from it: the test articles are PLA printed through a 0.30 mm nozzle (not CF-nylon through 0.6 mm); the sealing test is a bubble/volumetric test at about 0.5 bar overpressure, sensitive to roughly mL/s flows - 9-10 orders of magnitude coarser than a vacuum leak budget in the 1e-5 mbar.L/s class, so 'completely blocked' in this paper does not mean vacuum-tight; the k = 0.98 threshold and the wall-thickness series (~0.5 mm perimeter-only walls often untenable at any k; >= 1.1 mm walls seal via a homogeneous inner layer) are from one lab, one printer, one slicer. Caveats that ride on every number taken from it: the test articles are PLA printed through a 0.30 mm nozzle (not CF-nylon through 0.6 mm); the sealing test is a bubble/volumetric test at about 0.5 bar overpressure, sensitive to roughly mL/s flows - 9-10 orders of magnitude coarser than a vacuum leak budget in the 1e-5 mbar.L/s class, so 'completely blocked' in this paper does not mean vacuum-tight; the k = 0.98 threshold and the wall-thickness series (~0.5 mm perimeter-only walls often untenable at any k; >= 1.1 mm walls seal via a homogeneous inner layer) are from one lab, one printer, one slicer. One chapter of a larger annual publication; the DOI 10.3133/mcs2022 identifies the whole Mineral Commodity Summaries 2022, and [link] serves the helium chapter as this standalone PDF. The 2021 figures are marked estimated ('e') in the chapter itself, and the chapter's own footnote warns that Census Bureau export data for 2018-2021 'may be incorrect', with apparent consumption estimated at 40 Mm3/yr as a result. This is the baseline of the price series this project cites: $7.57/m3 is HE_PRICE_2021_USD_M3 in research/analysis/[link], the denominator of the +85%-in-two-years repricing. Note the wording: 'with some producers posting surcharges to this price' - the base price understates what buyers paid. One chapter of a larger annual publication; DOI 10.3133/mcs2024 identifies the whole Mineral Commodity Summaries 2024.
